content: In France, public hospitals fully cover prenatal and postnatal care through the social security system. Working women are eligible for 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily benefits varying from €9.29 to €84.90 depending on their previous earnings. Financial concerns during pregnancy and the surrounding periods remain on par with other life stages—low-income families continue to face challenges, but no more intensely than usual, while wealthier families maintain their standard of living. However, when it comes to actual support for new mothers, there is little in place. Paternity leave is limited to just 11 days, which falls short of allowing mothers adequate recovery time. As a result, new mothers are left to handle constant newborn care while still healing, all while searching for childcare options. State-supported programs are insufficient, particularly in the Paris area. Although nursery fees can be as low as €1,000 annually for lower-income families, there is only one available spot for every eight children. Consequently, many families turn to private childcare solutions like nannies or home-based care providers. Any other questions?
